title: Hark! What Mean Those Holy Voices
description: Hark! What Mean Those Holy Voices in Tonic Solfa to STUTTGART, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Cawood wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 160.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to STUTTGART; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! what mean those ho-ly voi-ces Sweet-ly sound-ing through the skies? Lo! th’an-gel-ic host re-joi-ces, Heav-enly hal-le-lu-jahs rise.

lines: Hark! what mean those holy voices
Sweetly sounding through the skies?
Lo! th’ angelic host rejoices,
Heavenly hallelujahs rise.
Listen to the wondrous story
Which they chant in hymns of joy,
Glory in the highest, glory!
Glory be to God most high!
Peace on earth, good will from heaven,
Reaching far as man is found;
Souls redeemed and sins forgiven!
Loud our golden harps shall sound.
Christ is born, the great Anointed;
Heaven and earth, His praises sing!
O receive whom God appointed
For your Prophet, Priest, and King.
Hasten, mortals, to adore Him,
Learn His name and taste His joy,
Till in heaven ye sing before Him,
Glory be to God most high!
Let us learn the wondrous story
Of our great Redeemer’s birth;
Spread the brightness of His glory
Till it cover all the earth.

licence: Public domain: John Cawood died in 1852.
credits: Words by John Cawood (1775–1852), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to STUTTGART by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
